messages:
alex: quick sync — we need to lock down SDK surface for pagination + retries across py/ts/go. proposal: two-tier API: a high-level iterator that retries and resumes, and a low-level raw pager that returns (items, next_token) and does no retries by default. thoughts?
mei: sounds reasonable. main concern is hidden retries in the iterator causing duplicate processing for non-idempotent handlers. we should surface an idempotency/at-least-once warning.
sanjay: +1 to two-tier. for go specifically, iterators are awkward (channels/goroutines) so prefer explicit pager that returns a struct with Next(ctx) that can return ResumeToken. but keep an ergonomic iterator for py/ts where generator/async iterators are idiomatic.
rina: also consider transport differences: http/1.1 chunked vs http2/grpc streaming. streaming can give resume per-chunk but many customers use our REST endpoints. do we bind retry semantics to transport or to SDK surface?
mei: i'd keep transport orthogonal. SDK should implement retries based on error classification (transient network, 5xx, 429) and idempotency hints from API (operation can be retried). transport choice only affects implementation details (e.g., we can stream tokens over http2).
sanjay: concretely: iterator behavior = auto-retry on transient errors up to N attempts with exponential backoff and jitter; when a retry happens, it should attempt to resume using the last seen resume_token. If resume_token missing, surface a retry error. that keeps semantics safe.
alex: good. proposal tweaks: default attempts=3, base_backoff=200ms, max_backoff=5s. iterator exposes params: disable_retries, max_attempts, on_retry hook, and resume_token getter. low-level pager returns (items, next_token) and never retries unless caller uses helpers.
mei: API example for py:
```
for item in client.list_objects(auto_retry=True, page_size=200):
    process(item)
```
and low-level:
```
items, token = client.list_objects_page(page_size=200, token=None)
```

sanjay: go shape suggestion:
```
type Pager struct { token string }
func (p *Pager) Next(ctx context.Context) ([]Item, string, error)
```
Next does at-most-one internal retry and returns a resume token. callers implement their own goroutine if they want streaming.
rina: about idempotency — server should include a header `x-next-resume-token` and `x-idempotency: retryable|non-retryable` so client can make informed decisions. infra-bot created RFC stub: <https://redwood.company/rfcs/pager-retries-280123>
infra-bot: RFC draft created by rina: https://redwood.company/rfcs/pager-retries-280123 (status: draft) :spiral_note_pad:
alex: decision summary: agreement on two-tier surface; iterator auto-retries up to 3 with resume_token use; low-level page API is retry-free; expose flags to opt-out and hooks for telemetry. go will prefer explicit pager.Next pattern; py/ts keep generator/async iterator ergonomics. server-side to add resume and idempotency headers. i'll update RFC and open PR for py/ts shape.
mei: please add test matrix in RFC: transports (rest/stream), error classes, resume-token loss scenarios, and language-specific semantics (sync/async).
sanjay: i'll take the Go PR (interface + tests).
rina: i'll update server header spec and add integration tests.
alex: thanks all — we'll reconvene after PRs land. :thumbsup:
